messages:
maya: FYI - ACME reported p99 spikes on Dedicated during their billing window. They saw spikes from ~1200ms to ~6s for a small burst of requests. Filing here to sync on short-term mitigation.
jonas: thanks. do we have pool id / customer id / any correlating alerts? :eyes:
maya: cust=acme-inc, pool=d-ed-42, spike started 11:40 UTC, ~450 concurrent attach attempts. alerts-bot: [ALERT] dedicated.attach.latency.p99 > 5s for pool d-ed-42 (11:40 - 11:50)
li: looking. initial suspicion is scale-up attach queueing + cold GPU starts. can you paste a couple of raw request ids or sample traces?
maya: sample request ids: r_3fa2, r_3fa3. customer says they were getting 429 then 500 then long tails. logs: ```
ERROR attach: attach_timeout pool=d-ed-42 id=r_3fa2 wait_ms=120005
WARN provisioner: image_pull slow, retrying (attempt 2)
```
priya: can you run the provisioning queue query? use this in grafana (panel): ```query: sum(rate(provisioner.queue_length{pool=\"d-ed-42\"}[1m])) by (reason)``` seeing sustained queueing would confirm attach-starvation.
li: ran quick look - queue_length had a 1m spike to 380 at 11:41, p95 attach duration matches ~5.6s. also seeing increased cold_gpu_start events with image_pull > 20s.
priya: short-term mitigation: bump min_in_flight for d-ed-42 or increase prewarm target. command to tweak: `redwoodctl pools update d-ed-42 --min-prewarm 6` (ops permission required). alternatively route high-priority customers to hosted fallback for the window: `routes update --match cust=acme-inc --fallback hosted`
jonas: can we do both? prewarm + fallback for critical endpoints. who has perms to run redwoodctl?
maya: i can escalate to infra-ops, pinging @li and @priya to do config change if we confirm.
li: i'll raise min-prewarm to 6 for now and watch. will also disable aggressive fairshare for a short window so acme's queued attaches don't starve. running: `redwoodctl pools patch d-ed-42 --set fairshare.enabled=false`
alerts-bot: [ACTION] pool d-ed-42 config changed: min-prewarm=6, fairshare.enabled=false (by li)
sam: customer notified? we should tell them we're doing prewarm + fallback and ask for a low-traffic test window. i'll DM their CSM and post an update now.
maya: noted. will follow up with postmortem template after we stabilize. please collect kube logs for those attach failures and image_pull latencies.
priya: follow-up action: run image registry health check and pre-pull most common images to reduce cold starts. I'll file infra ticket: INFRA-1192.
li: monitoring note - if p99 doesn't drop within 15m, plan B is to shift some capacity from EU-dedicated to this pool (manual) and revert fairshare changes after window.
jonas: thanks all. next update in 10m. :thumbsup:
maya: update - p99 dropped to ~900ms after prewarm change and fallback enabled. closing this thread once infra ticket and PM communication are in place.
